Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The Sri Lankan players are in a huddle with their skipper giving final words of motivation before his troops take the field. Lendl Simmons and Evin Lewis walk out to open the innings for West Indies. The visitors will start with spin as Akila Dananjaya is set to operate with the new ball.

So 132 is what West Indies need to win the series. With the batting lineup they have, one would believe it to be achieved but the powerhouse West Indies batting has not been at its best in this series. Sri Lanka would have liked to have a bit more after opting to bat but they have something to bowl at. They will look to repeat their heroics from the last game and finally get a T20I series win. Can the tourists do the magic or will the hosts get the job done?

The star of West Indies' bowling, Fabian Allen is caught for a quick chat. On the caught and bowled, Allen says that it was all about execution. On bowling in the Powerplay, Allen says that the skipper asked him to do so and he did that. Tells that they have a good batting unit and hopes that they will chase it down.

Superb bowling display from West Indies. They looked up for the task from ball one and the ploy to start with spinners paid dividends. Allen and Sinclair started with the new ball and the pair grabbed sent both the openers packing. Fabian Allen was the star with the ball, finishing with 1/13 from his 4. McCoy and Holder bowled well for their one wicket a piece as well. Sinclair and Bravo were a touch expensive but overall it was an impressive showing from the hosts.

After opting to bat, Sri Lanka started off terribly as they lost their top 3 batters inside the Powerplay with very little on the board. Skipper, Angelo Mathews too did not last long. It looked like the tourists would strugggle to get 120 but Chandimal held on like a glue and found an able partner in Bandara. The pair added 85 with Chandimal getting to his fifty. This partnership ensured that Sri Lanka have a respectable total.

Excellent bowling display from West Indies. They have bowled and fielded fantastically in the first half of this game and now the onus will be on the batters. Sri Lanka have something to bowl at and they will be satisfied as they have something to bowl at and one can never be sure as this pitch does not look easy to bat on.

OUT! CAUGHT! Superb catch from Sinclair and the West Indies players look in the groove and up for it tonight. Nissanka never looked settled and this seemed to be coming. Holder hits the deck hard on middle. Nissanka makes room and looks to flat-bat it over mid off. He mistimes it and hits it high in the air. Sinclair runs behind, keeps his eyes on the ball, and takes it brilliantly in the end falling down to the ground. End of the Powerplay and it has clearly belonged to the hosts. Sri Lanka off to a stuttering start. They are 27/3 after the end of the Powerplay.

OUT! CAUGHT! Kevin Sinclair brings out the somersault and West Indies are off to a fantastic start. Terrible for Sri Lanka as they have lost two wickets inside the Powerplay itself with another couple remaining. Flattish delivery on off, Dickwella looks to go for a big sweep. He mistimes it and hits it high in the air. Holder moves to his left from mid on and takes a good catch. Sinclair does the dangerous somersault perfectly and he is a happy man.

OUT! CAUGHT! Excellent catch from Fabian Allen! This is a top drawer from Allen. He is a gun fielder and this is a gun catch. Floated on off, Allen gives this ball some air. Gunathilaka hits it straught but uppishly to the left of Allen. He outstretches his hand and takes a one-handed stunner to give West Indies an early breakthrough. Just the kind of start the hosts would have wanted.
Floated on off, Gunathilaka milks it through mid off and keeps the strike.

Risky run but Gunathilaka is in! A better throw might have been dangerous. Shorter on off, Gunathilaka punches it to the left of  point and calls for a run.They go for it. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but Sinclair cannot collect the ball.

Tight start! Just a single off the over. The last ball is short on off, Pathum Nissanka punches it to cover.

Sri Lanka and Gunathilaka are off the mark. Short around off, Gunathilaka cuts it to short third man and takes a quick single to get the first run of the evening.

Allen starts with a floated delivery around off, Gunathilaka hits it hard but straight to the man at short extra cover.

We are all set for the action to begin! The West Indies players are out in the middle. They are followed by the Sri Lankan opening pair of Pathum Nissanka and Danushka Gunathilaka! West Indies are all set to start with spin. The players before the start take a knee in solidarity against racism. Fabian Allen is set to start the proceedings with the new ball.

PITCH REPORT -  Darren Ganga and Shakera Selman are the pitch analysts for the day. Selman says this is a new pitch and expects it to be good for both batting and bowling. She feels there will be some help for the spinners as it is drier. Ganga tells Sri Lanka spinners have bowled well. Selman feels West Indies need to put on their dancing shoes against Wanindu and also bring out the sweep.

West Indies skipper, Kieron Pollard, says that they have discussions about the spinners in Sri Lanka. Tells the guys need to take responsibility. Informs Edwards misses out and Powell comes in. Tells they expected spin in the back end as that is their combination. Pollard feels they have a good chance. Hopes to restrict them under 160 and chase it down.

Sri Lanka skipper, Angelo Mathews, informs they are unchanged. Mathews says that they have been unable to deliver but tells today is a big opportunity and hopes they can put runs against this world-class side. Mathews tells they can improve in all departments especially with the bat between overs 7-15.

Sri Lanka (Unchanged Playing XI) - Danushka Gunathilaka, Pathum Nissanka, Dinesh Chandimal, Angelo Mathews (C), Ashen Bandara, Thisara Perera, Wanindu Hasaranga, Niroshan Dickwella (WK), Akila Dananjaya, Lakshan Sandakan, Dushmantha Chameera.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Lendl Simmons, Evin Lewis, Chris Gayle, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Kieron Pollard (C), Jason Holder, Rovman Powell (IN FOR FIDEL EDWARDS), Fabian Allen, Dwayne Bravo, Kevin Sinclair, Obed McCoy.
TOSS - Time for the coin flip. Both the skippers are out in the middle for the coin flip. Up goes the coin and comes down in favour of the visitors. SRI LANKA OPT TO BAT!

Hello and welcome to the third and final T20I between West Indies and Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka, have ended their winless streak and now will look to carry the winning momentum, seal the series and surprise the rest of the cricketing world. West Indies, will be desperate to put the grief of the last game and win the series. They struggled against the spinners and Kieron Pollard will hope his star batters finally deliver at this critical juncture. Can Sri Lanka spin another surprise or will West Indies win the series?
